The successive CDW states observed in the NbSe$_3$ system with respect to the arrival of x-ray pulses follow a non-thermal kinetic path. It is characterized by a change in 2k$_F$ wavevector, correlation lengths and electronic gap, as well as a change of dimensionality, all of this takes place within a very long recovery time ranging from 450$ns$ to 0.01$s$. Several scenarios are proposed, including transient nucleation and recombination of charged topological objects.

title: Hydrodynamic description of correlation matrix eigenvalues in a finite temperature expanding free fermionic gas
summary: A recent work considered the Page curve for entanglement entropy of a freely expanding one-dimensional Fermi gas starting from a finite box (the system) in a zero-temperature initial state that then expands in to a semi-infinite vacuum (the environment). For the case with a single defect at the system-environment junction, it was shown that the Yang-Yang entropy of the system computed from semiclassical hydrodynamics agrees with the microscopically computed entanglement entropy, yielding the Page curve. On the other hand, the environment Yang-Yang entropy showed a monotonic increase. Here, we propose a hydrodynamic description to obtain the eigenvalues of the microscopic correlation matrix for a nonzero temperature freely-expanding Fermi gas. For the system, the phase space density directly gives the correlation matrix eigenvalues and thus, via the Yang-Yang formula, yields the von-Neumann entropy. For the reservoir, a modification of the phase space density is required in the Yang-Yang formula, to incorporate coherences, in order to reproduce accurately the entropy. The hydrodynamic description of correlation matrix eigenvalues also leads to a Levitov-Lesovik type formula for the full-counting-statistics for a finite system in the transient regime. We provide a heuristic derivation of the correlation matrix eigenvalues based on a semiclassical wave-packet picture.

title: Readout Dependent Parameter Identifiability of Quantum Kernels
comment: 53 pages, 3 figures. Includes appendices. Code and reproducibility materials: https://github.com/parkfinity/readout_kernel_identifiability
summary: A circuit parameter can change measured features without changing their projected Gaussian kernel. We characterize this lost dependence and distinguish recovery by metric design from nonlinear feature expansion. With analytic feature coefficients, a fixed finite data basis affinely independent on the input domain, a fixed positive definite metric, and fixed bandwidth, the coefficient Gram matrix determines all-input kernel equivalence, global coordinate inactivity, and generic differential rank. An exact four-qubit family exhibits a sharp boundary: diagonal metrics give rank two, dense metrics reach but cannot exceed three, and no fixed affine expansion crosses this ceiling. One appended nonlinear scalar coordinate suffices for rank four and is minimal when the original features are retained. A single pairwise product achieves this with an explicit nondiagonal metric; a scalar sum of two products achieves it with a diagonal metric. Both use existing ideal local means. Exact certificates establish ranks in 54 selected circuit/readout settings. Matched finite-shot comparisons show that minimal representation size need not give the best sensitivity among the tested designs. Under a factorized measurement distribution, conditional product estimation cannot increase variance at a fixed design. Execution audits further separate kernel identifiability from compiled cost.

title: Stabilizing and detecting electron fractionalization in the Hofstadter-Hubbard model
summary: Motivated by the recent progress in correlated Chern insulator physics in moiré systems, we investigate the half-filled triangular-lattice Hofstadter--Hubbard model and its electron fractionalization. Among various competing non-magnetic states, increasing the orbital flux stabilizes and broadens the $\mathrm{U}(1)_2$ chiral spin liquid phase in the Mott regime. In this exotic regime, the electron is fractionalized into gapped spinons and gapped chargons, whose effective bands are linked to the orbital flux. The convolution of the narrow spinon bands with the gapped chargon excitations produces rich and discernible structures in the electron spectral function and the density of states. These results not only identify the orbital flux as a control parameter for the detailed patterns of electron fractionalization and the nature of the Mott transition, but also provide the key spectral characteristics for the angle-resolved photoemission and scanning tunneling studies of the relevant systems, linking the free-particle band topology to intrinsic topological order in the correlated regime.

title: Alignment of the amplitudes of stored states for solving the associative memory problem using quantum annealing
summary: The solution of combinatorial optimization problems by means of quantum annealing is based on the preparation of an equally superposition state. Such superposition is crucial to the associative memory problem of correctly recalling patterns. In this paper, we study the alignment of the amplitudes of stored states in memory using the proposed auxiliary Hamiltonian, which is switched off at the end of evolution. The results of the algorithm execution were obtained both by numerical modeling and by the perturbation theory method, which made it possible to obtain the dependences on physical parameters in explicit form. As examples, systems of two and three qutrits, represented by spins S=1, are considered. Since the Hamiltonian is expressed in a univer-sal form through projectors onto states stored in memory, it can be used for other quantum sys-tems (platforms).

title: Projective symmetry groups beyond spin-$1/2$: Classifying integer-spin quantum spin liquids
summary: Wen's projective symmetry group (PSG), introduced a quarter of a century ago, reduced the classification of symmetric quantum spin liquids to an algebraic problem and has guided the study of spin-$1/2$ models and materials ever since. Many current candidate materials and quantum simulators, however, have spin-$1$ or larger moments, and no comparable classification exists for them. We formulate the PSG for fermionic partons of arbitrary spin $S$. Integer and half-odd-integer spins already differ in their gauge structure. Half-odd-integer spins give the familiar $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, $\mathrm{U}(1)$, and $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant gauge groups, while integer spins give a different hierarchy that includes $\mathrm{U}(1)\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_2$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$; the latter has no spin-$1/2$ counterpart. Three lattice-independent results follow for integer spin. Singlet pairing of the partons is odd under site exchange. A lattice symmetry can exchange the particle and hole representations of the local constraint, which forces symmetry-related sites into opposite constraint sectors. And a time-reversal-symmetric $\mathrm{U}(1)$ state with the same constraint on every site can be gapped only if the number of sites per unit cell is a multiple of $2S+1$. We apply the formalism to the spin-$1$ diamond lattice, realized in frustrated A-site spinels, and find ten fully symmetric Ansätze up to second neighbors. In the $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg model at the mean-field level, the ground state depends on how the constraint is imposed. With the particle and hole representations, the lowest states are fully gapped $\mathrm{U}(1)$ states whose two sublattices sit in opposite constraint sectors, and one of them is gauge equivalent to a paired Ansatz. The classification provides a starting point for integer-spin quantum spin liquids on other lattices and in other materials.

title: PQ-Vault: Provably Quantum-Safe Asset Custody for Unmodified Ethereum
summary: A quantum computer could recover the key of any Ethereum account whose public key appears on chain. We prove that no sidechain or bridge that leaves Ethereum's rules unchanged can protect such accounts: their funds must move into a contract whose release condition relies only on quantum-safe primitives. We design \emph{PQ-Vault}, a custody system for unmodified Ethereum combining this vault, a quantum-safe proof-of-stake sidechain whose checkpoints carry compact certificates, and an optimistic dispute protocol. We give the first security proof of compact certificates against quantum attackers and a matching attack: with classically chosen parameters, the guarantee falls from 128 to about 60 bits, and a simple rule restores it. We show that a common seed-update rule in hash-chain proof of stake lets an attacker steer chosen slots and profit from splitting its stake, and give an election whose steering gain and inclusion delay are provably bounded against quantum attackers. Since compressing certificates with a pairing-based SNARK breaks quantum security, we use fraud proofs that need a single signature check. For 65,536 validators, a certificate is 0.8 MB, 260 times smaller than all signatures, and verifies in about 20 ms; the vault accepts a checkpoint for about 420,000 gas.

title: An Instability of the Quantum Markov Length
comment: 5 Pages + Appendices, 3 Figures, Added `Note Added' section + minor adjustments
summary: The Markov length, the length scale governing the exponential decay of conditional mutual information (CMI) in a quantum many-body state, has proven useful for characterizing mixed-state phases of matter. Nevertheless, we show that a state's Markov length is not generally stable under weak local channels. The failure of stability occurs already at a pure product state. We demonstrate this explicitly in a one-dimensional fermionic chain, where a fine-tuned depth-two circuit of nearest-neighbor Gaussian channels maps the vacuum to a state whose CMI decays \emph{algebraically} and whose Markov length is therefore infinite, even when the channels are taken arbitrarily close to the identity. The algebraic decay is rooted in the nonanalyticity of the von Neumann entropy at rank-deficient density operators. We exhibit an analogous instability on an ordinary qubit chain. More generally, we show that the Markov length is unstable in any translation-invariant state with even a single rank-deficient reduced density operator. These results pose a challenge to recent definitions of mixed-state phase equivalence based on the Markov length.

title: Low-field dephasing time of an optically polarized NV$^-$ spin bath beyond the P1 limit in diamond: a cluster-correlation-expansion and exact spin-bath study
summary: Dense ensembles of nitrogen-vacancy (NV$^-$) centres in nitrogen-rich diamond dephase on the electron spins of the substitutional nitrogen (P1) centres. If the paramagnetic nitrogen is instead converted into NV$^-$ centres, the laser that initializes the sensor also pumps the bath into $m_s$ = 0, a state with no moment along its own axis. Using cluster-correlation-expansion (CCE) calculations, combined with an exact solver for probe-bath exchange and with no adjustable parameter, this paper asks whether such an optically polarized NV$^-$ bath dephases a sensor more slowly than a P1 bath of the same density. The answer is set by the field. In a field along [111], three quarters of the bath centres lie off the field axis, and the moment of their $m_s$ = 0 state along the field grows from 0.04 at 25 G to 0.46 at 300 G and 0.81 at 800 G. At 25 G the polarized bath is therefore nearly silent: at $10^{17}$ cm$^{-3}$ the dephasing time $T_2^*$ of a separately addressed $^{15}$NV$^-$ probe is 112 us, six times the 18.1 us of a P1 bath, and still 2.4 times at 90 % polarization; an ensemble measurement gains a factor of two. At 300 G the advantage over P1 shrinks to 1.4, and at 800 G the polarized bath dephases faster than P1. The field dependence of every bath, P1 included, follows the mean moment of its centres along the field. For the Hahn echo, exchange with on-axis bath centres and bath relaxation ($T_1$ = 6 ms) limit the gain to 1.2 times the P1 value at 25 G. Optical polarization of an NV$^-$ bath at low field therefore offers dephasing times beyond the P1 limit of nitrogen-rich diamond.

title: Liouvillian Non-Invertible Symmetry
comment: 12 pages, 3 figures, 1 table. Includes End Matter and Supplemental Material
summary: Non-invertible symmetries extend conventional symmetries beyond group-like transformations and play an important role in quantum field theory and many-body physics. However, a general framework of non-invertible symmetries in open quantum systems is still lacking. Here, we formulate a general Liouville-space duality framework that extends Hilbert-space non-invertible dualities to open quantum systems. The resulting defect relates Liouvillians with dual Hamiltonian and dissipative parameters and becomes an exact symmetry at self-duality. We apply this framework to the periodic transverse-field Ising chain with two collective Lindblad channels exchanged by Kramers--Wannier (KW) duality. A strong $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry divides Liouville space into four parity sectors, while the defect acts nontrivially only in the even-even sector. At self-duality, the KW defect imposes a momentum-resolved selection rule on Liouvillian Jordan blocks. Modes with different Liouville momenta or KW-defect eigenvalues cannot form a common exceptional Jordan block. For a three-site chain, a global Rényi-2 KW asymmetry dynamically identifies the self-dual conditions. At the same time, the spectral structure exhibits both a semisimple degeneracy and a self-dual exceptional point with a perturbation-selective response. These results extend non-invertible dualities to Markovian quantum dynamics and establish a symmetry-based selection rule for Liouvillian Jordan structures.

title: Boundary exceptional point driven chiral switch of topological edge states
summary: We theoretically investigate the interplay of topology and localized non-Hermiticity in a finite Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain characterized by non-Hermitian potentials at its boundaries. By tuning the boundary gain and loss parameters, we exploit the finite-size hybridization of two mid-gap topological edge states to analytically derive the exact coordinates of boundary-induced exceptional points (EPs), $Γ_{\rm EP}=\pm i v^{N}/w^{N-1}$, at which these states undergo coalescence. We demonstrate that dynamically encircling these boundary EPs facilitates a robust, chiral edge state-transfer protocol. Depending on the orientation of the encircling loop, this protocol allows a topological edge state localized at one boundary to be either transferred to the opposite edge with perfect fidelity or returned to its starting position through a double switching process. Importantly, since the non-Hermiticity remains strictly confined to the boundaries, this chiral transport occurs without affecting the energy spectrum of the bulk bands. These results establish a minimal framework for a large-scale topological chiral switch that is experimentally verifiable and capable of being controlled through boundary non-Hermitian driving.

title: Dynamical Tunneling Blockade in Layer-Pseudospin Ferromagnets
summary: Double-layer systems with narrow or flat electronic bands may exhibit spontaneous interlayer coherence, described by a layer-pseudospin ferromagnetic order parameter. In modern realizations of layer-pseudospin ferromagnets, the electrons carry additional valley degeneracies, endowing each layer with a valley-pseudospin degree of freedom. We study their nonequilibrium steady states driven by a static interlayer voltage bias in the presence of interlayer tunneling. While in the low-bias regime, the system is in a static state with parallel valley pseudospins between the two layers, we show that in the high-bias regime, the dynamical precession of the layer-pseudospin stabilizes the valley pseudospins in the antiparallel configuration, strongly suppressing the interlayer tunneling. This dynamical tunneling blockade leads to an absence of ac current and a sharp drop of the dc tunneling current to a tiny value, in stark contrast to conventional quantum Hall double layers.

title: Adapted Fröhlich-Pizzo Model for Horizon-Induced Decoherence
summary: The Fröhlich-Pizzo (FP) model is a quantum-mechanical model originally developed to describe the interaction between an atom and the electromagnetic field in the nonrelativistic limit $c\to\infty$. We show that an adaptation of the FP model based on the local algebras of a $U(1)$ chiral current captures essential features of the horizon-induced decoherence mechanism identified by Danielson, Satishchandran, and Wald (DSW) in the limit of large holding time $T$. Our analysis suggests that the effective dynamics of the system undergoing decoherence in the DSW setting retains non-Markovian features. Our approach also offers a glimpse into the possible role of quantum events in the dynamics underlying horizon-induced decoherence.

title: Quantum Simulation of Non-Markovian Open Quantum Systems via Low-Rank Kernel Compression and Coupling Dilution
summary: We present an error-controlled framework for the quantum simulation of non-Markovian open-system dynamics in Gaussian environments. For a system coupled linearly to a Gaussian environment with zero mean, the bath's influence on the reduced dynamics is completely determined by its two-time correlation kernel. This allows us to replace the microscopic environment with an equivalent bath that has the same kernel. On a finite simulation interval, a rank-$N$ approximation of the kernel yields an effective bath of $N$ bosonic modes with time-dependent couplings to the system. To encode these modes in qubits, we first truncate each mode to its lowest $d$ occupation levels. When stronger couplings lead to large occupations, we introduce coupling dilution, which replaces each mode with several more weakly coupled copies while preserving the bath correlation kernel. This distributes excitations across more modes and trades additional modes for smaller local dimensions. We derive explicit reduced-state error bounds and establish polynomial circuit width and depth in simulation time and inverse accuracy under stated spectral-decay and coupling-regularity assumptions, provided elementary unitaries admit polynomial-cost implementations.

title: Convergence Analysis of the Quantum Blahut-Arimoto Algorithm and the Contraction Coefficient of Qubit Amplitude-Damping Channels
summary:
In this work, we investigate the convergence rate of the quantum Blahut-Arimoto (BA) algorithm proposed for computing the coherent information of less noisy quantum channels. Previous work established exponential convergence under certain restrictive assumptions on the channel. Using a Taylor expansion around a positive definite optimizer, we show that, for an injective degradable channel whose degrading channel has a relative-entropy contraction coefficient strictly less than one, the algorithm converges at an exponential rate after sufficiently many iterations. We further verify this condition for qubit amplitude-damping (AD) channels in the relevant parameter regime.
  In addition, by analyzing the Bogoliubov-Kubo-Mori (BKM) metric on the Bloch ball, we derive an explicit characterization of the relative-entropy contraction coefficient of qubit AD channels. The proposed approach is further extended to calculate the relative contraction coefficient and the relative expansion coefficient of two qubit AD channels.

title: Bounds on Attainable Rate Modulation in Fermi's Golden Rule
summary: Controlling transition rates is a central objective across quantum optics, condensed-matter physics, and chemical physics, encompassing processes such as spontaneous emission, energy and charge transfer, spin relaxation, and chemical reactions. Although Fermi's golden rule provides a powerful framework for calculating such rates of weakly coupled transitions, conventional calculations require the interaction to be specified in advance; the range of rate responses attainable over a broader interaction space remains unknown. We formulate spectral-overlap golden-rule rates as quadratic forms of the interaction and derive rigorous bounds on rate modulation over a specified interaction space. As an example, application to energy transfer from a donor to a molecular vibration coupled to an optical cavity reveals that enhancement and suppression depend jointly on the interaction and cavity detuning, including continuous reversal of the rate response for a fixed interaction. The same approach may elucidate rate control for other golden-rule processes, including excitation-energy transfer, nonadiabatic electron transfer, nonradiative electronic transitions, vibrational and spin relaxation, and spontaneous emission.

title: Photon Correlations Control Quantum Fisher Information in Coherent Multidimensional Spectroscopy
summary: Coherent multidimensional spectroscopy probes interactions and dynamics of molecular systems through nonlinear optical signals. Quantum light excitation has been explored as a means of controlling these signals, raising the question of how excitation-light correlations affect the precision of molecular parameter estimation from the emitted signal. In this work, we show that photon-number correlations and two-photon coherence play distinct roles in encoding molecular information in the emitted rephasing signal. In the weak-emission regime and within the single Schmidt pair approximation, we derive a normally ordered information law in which the joint photon-number moment and the squared magnitude of the two-photon coherence weight the amplitude and phase sensitivities of the molecular response, respectively. For matched temporal modes and mean photon numbers in each input mode, two-mode squeezed vacuum enhances both weights relative to coherent excitation, whereas independent displaced squeezing preserves the amplitude weight but reduces the phase weight. The background population and its parameter dependence also affect the total quantum Fisher information, which therefore cannot be inferred from the coherent mean-field signal alone. We derive a leading-order bound on its enhancement over coherent excitation when the background population is nonnegative and common to the compared sources. These findings provide criteria for selecting excitation sources according to how the target molecular parameter affects the amplitude and phase of the response.

title: Quantum Belief Characterization: A Multi-Shot Notion of Equivalence
summary: A recent formulation of quantum belief showed that quantum retrodiction depends not only on the reduced density operator of the system of interest, but also on correlations with a hidden reference system, which leads to the notion of quantum belief equivalence. In this paper we formulate a multi-shot problem, where the extended posterior obtained after one update is used again as the prior for the next update. We first define a formal notion of $n$-shot equivalence and derive several propositions for arbitrary extended beliefs. We then argue that the agent must also specify why the data obtained in different rounds concern the same underlying object. Through the quantum de Finetti representation, this narrows the one-copy belief to a special class: candidate-state ensemble belief. In that sector, we show that two beliefs are $n$-shot equivalent if and only if their $(n+1)$-th moments are equal. We also give a physical interpretation of this moment condition and illustrate it through the equivalence between Haar priors and projective-design priors at bounded update depth.

title: Short qudit triorthogonal codes from doubling
summary: We construct short triorthogonal codes for qudits of odd prime dimension by generalizing doubling, which combines a triorthogonal code with a code admitting a transversal phase gate, and raises the distance by up to two. This gives codes with parameters $[[28,1,4]]_3$, $[[37,1,5]]_3$, $[[72,1,6]]_3$, $[[118,1,8]]_3$, $[[33,1,5]]_5$ and $[[20,1,4]]_7$, each shorter than the cyclic, concatenated and Reed-Muller codes of the same distance, and a doubling construction of the $[[15,1,3]]_3$ code. When the columns of a generator matrix are regarded as charged points, triorthogonality becomes the vanishing of multipole moments up to octupole order, and doubling becomes a double layer of opposite charges; this picture explains why inputs with nontrivial coefficients can give shorter codes. We also show by exhaustive search that the shortest codes of distance three have length $11$ for $p=5$ and length $7$ for $p=7$. Combined with high-rate distance-two codes, the new codes reduce the cost of qutrit magic state distillation by up to an order of magnitude in regimes with high input noise.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Matterwave Interferometry in a Ring Waveguide
summary: We propose a quantum-enhanced matter-wave interferometry protocol based on fractional-revival dynamics of a Bose-Einstein condensate in a ring, combined with a controlled interaction quench. Using the Truncated Wigner Approximation, we show that nonlinear evolution to the quarter revival generates modest spin squeezing of $-2.03\pm0.28\;$dB, which subsequently degrades under further nonlinear evolution. In contrast, starting from a non-interacting condensate, a controlled interaction quench applied after the initial quarter-revival beam-splitter operation generates substantially stronger spin squeezing of $-14.57\pm0.27\;$dB. We further show that phase control at $t=3T_r/8$ rotates the squeezed quadrature onto the phase-sensitive direction $\hat{J}_y$, producing a phase-squeezed state at $t=T_r/2$. The subsequent quarter-revival evolution converts this phase-squeezed state into a number-squeezed state, enabling population-difference readout. The resulting sequence provides a route to quantum-enhanced interferometry using the intrinsic fractional-revival dynamics of a ring together with controlled interaction and phase operations.

title: Local distinguishability of five quadripartite orthogonal product states
summary: The local distinguishability of five bipartite and tripartite orthogonal product states (OPSs) has been effectively resolved, while that of five quadripartite OPSs has not yet been effectively addressed. In this paper, we give the local distinguishability of five quadripartite OPSs, where any two of these five states are orthogonal on exactly one subsystem. Based on the vectors of the numbers of pairwise orthogonality relations, we classify different sets of five quadripartite OPSs into nine categories, which correspond to 371 distinct orthogonality graphs. We show that the sets of five quadripartite OPSs corresponding to 355 of the 371 cases can be perfectly distinguished by local operations and classical communication (LOCC), whereas the sets of five quadripartite OPSs for the remaining 16 cases cannot exactly distinguished by LOCC. Our results enrich the theory of nonlocality for sets of OPSs.

title: Quantum f-divergences from retrodiction: a unifying classical variational principle
comment: 18 pages, 2 figures; preliminary version, comments welcome; 100th arXiv post
summary: The same classical f-divergence admits inequivalent extensions to quantum states. The question is whether these extensions can be obtained from a common operational variational principle. Here we generalize Matsumoto's reverse-test optimization by introducing a reference prior state. More explicitly, we minimize the statistical distinguishability between a forward and a reverse prepare-and-measure process, related by retrodiction through the chosen reference and subject to prescribed quantum averages. Distinguishability is quantified by the classical f-divergence between their complete records. For faithful states in finite dimension, we prove that the same spectral implementation attains the minimum simultaneously for every operator-convex f. Varying the reference allows us to interpolate between standard and maximal quantum f-divergences of the prescribed states, passing through the geodesic family. More precisely, a flat reference yields the standard quantum f-divergences, thereby giving the Nussbaum-Szkoła distributions a variational characterization as optimal records. Choosing either prescribed state as reference recovers maximal quantum f-divergences and Matsumoto's reverse tests, while power references realize the geodesic interpolation. In the relative-entropy case, this gives the passage from Umegaki to Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy by changing the prior for retrodiction.

title: Semiclassical molecular dynamics simulations of electromagnetically induced transparency cooling of 2D and 3D ion crystals in a Penning trap
summary: Motional modes of trapped-ion crystals in Penning traps can now be cooled to near their ground states via electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) cooling. Numerical simulations are valuable tools for interpreting EIT cooling results and optimizing experimental protocols, but existing molecular dynamics codes are limited to the simulation of Doppler cooling. In this work, we fill this gap by implementing a semiclassical model of EIT cooling in a novel MD code. By simultaneously evolving the ions' internal quantum states and classical motion, we are able to calculate the instantaneous EIT laser forces acting on the ions. We first validate our code by comparing the single-ion cooling rate to fully quantum simulation results. Next, we analyze cooling of the drumhead modes in planar ion crystals, quantifying the effects of planar ion motion and a finite laser beam width. Finally, we demonstrate efficient EIT cooling of the axial modes in 3D ellipsoidal crystals containing up to 500 ions. Such crystals are a promising platform for future quantum sensing experiments with enhanced sensitivity. We find that the mode spectra of 3D crystals can be engineered to enable sympathetic cooling of the low-frequency $\boldsymbol{E}\times\boldsymbol{B}$ modes. This numerical framework provides a powerful tool for modeling sub-Doppler cooling techniques and for optimizing future quantum sensing and quantum information experiments.

title: Encoding a bosonic mode into qubits for simulating boson-matter interactions
summary: We explore the space-time cost of encoding of a bosonic mode into a set of qubits via various encodings, and their resilience to noise. In particular, we compare the performance of the unary Fock state encoding, an unexplored encoding of Fock states into Dicke states (``Dicke'' encoding), and the binary quadrature encoding. We do so by considering a displacement as well as a simulation of a Dicke model, coupling a bosonic mode to a set of atoms represented as qubits. Using classical simulations, we assess the accuracy and optimized space-time costs in terms of number of qubits, circuit depth and CNOT count of a quantum simulation of the time dynamics using these encodings. Although our study is far from comprehensive, we find that the binary quadrature encoding is overall most favorable in terms of being very space-efficient and relatively time-efficient due to the use of the quantum Fourier transform. Our novel Dicke encoding leads to very shallow circuits, but pays in terms of using many more qubits. We probe the use of an H2-2 Quantinuum trapped-ion qubit device (56 qubits) for displacement and Dicke model simulation in the low boson-number regime, where we find that noise leads to visible deviations from ideal circuit dynamics.

title: Conservation in Every Quantum Measurement Outcome?
summary: In quantum mechanics, conservation laws are usually understood only statistically and only in the context of unitary evolution: during such evolution, if an observable commutes with the Hamiltonian, its expectation value and Born-rule probability distribution remain unchanged. Individual measurement outcomes, however, disrupt even this weak form of statistical conservation. Recently, though, it has been argued that a stronger, non-statistical form of conservation, valid at the level of individual measurement outcomes, can be recovered. The proposal relies on the claim that any superposition of eigenstates of a conserved quantity must ultimately be prepared relative to another physical system, which serves as the relevant reference frame and remains correlated with the system being prepared. On this enlarged description, the change observed in the measured system is claimed to be exactly compensated by an opposite change in the preparer, thereby restoring conservation at the level of individual measurement outcomes. We analyze this proposal and argue that it faces significant conceptual difficulties. We show that the proposed mechanism is not adequately justified and, moreover, does not establish conservation in individual measurement outcomes as claimed.

title: Superconducting parametric amplifiers based on arrays of unequal Josephson junction elements
comment: 15 pages, 8 figures, main text and appendices
summary: Impedance matching is a crucial feature of an amplifier used to increase its instantaneous bandwidth and is typically achieved using static LC resonators. Here we show an approach to impedance matching in parametric amplifiers using arrays of unequal Josephson-junction-based elements (rf/dc SQUIDs, SNAILs, etc). The elements act either as small-footprint flux-tunable inductors forming an impedance-matching circuit, or 'active' amplifier elements which result in amplifier gain. We develop an analytical theory describing these systems, predicting a quasi-non-periodic amplifier frequency and gain modulation with applied flux and the broadening of gain bandwidths. We demonstrate this in devices using arrays of flux-focused SNAILs where flux biasing varies across the array. We find instantaneous bandwidths of 200 MHz with $>$17 dB of gain centred at $\sim$5.4 GHz in a device without a static impedance matcher. This broadening of amplifier bandwidth is stable with $>$100 MHz bandwidth at 17 dB gain across $>$1.2 GHz tunable bandwidth. Our analytical model captures flux dependence and qualitatively reproduces gain-bandwidths giving confidence in our understanding of these systems and allowing operational figures of merit to be optimised in future devices.

title: Resource Analysis of Quantum Optimization Algorithms via Variational Methods
summary: Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQAs) are promising approaches for solving combinatorial optimization problems on near-term quantum devices. However, the role played by quantum resources such as entanglement and coherence during the optimization process remains poorly understood. In this work, we investigate the evolution of these resources in two VQAs--the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) and the Feedback-based Algorithm for Quantum Optimization (FALQON)--applied to the Minimum Vertex Cover problem. We employ a variational resource-quantification framework based on the Bures metric and Uhlmann's theorem, in which an auxiliary quantum circuit is optimized to identify the closest resource-free states. This approach allows us to quantify Bures entanglement and Bures coherence of the algorithmic states without requiring full quantum state tomography. For the considered problem instance, QAOA exhibits a pronounced accumulation of entanglement in its initial layers, followed by a progressive reduction as the algorithm converges toward the optimal solution. Its coherence likewise decreases overall with increasing circuit depth, although a finite residual value persists due to the degeneracy of the optimal-solution subspace. In contrast, FALQON exhibits a substantially lower entanglement peak, reached at larger circuit depth, followed by a decay as convergence proceeds. Its coherence decreases smoothly and monotonically together with the optimization error. These results reveal distinct quantum-resource trajectories associated with the two optimization strategies and illustrate how entanglement and coherence evolve as variational quantum states approach solutions of a classical combinatorial optimization problem.

title: Finite Classification of Transversal Diagonal Gates Beyond Stabilizer Codes
summary: We establish that transversal diagonal gates on exact qubit codes of distance at least two can be exhaustively classified within a finite search space. Although code-preserving physical gates can have continuous phases, any projective logical action induced by a transversal diagonal gate can always be realized by a physical gate of finite order. Crucially, we prove that this physical order has an upper bound determined solely by the code parameters. This order bound enables the subset-sum-linear-programming (SSLP) framework introduced in arXiv:2504.20847 to exhaustively enumerate all candidate discrete symmetries, after which the Knill-Laflamme equations determine the remaining continuous code parameters. Applying this method to the nontrivial diagonal sector of exact $((6,2,3))$ codes, SSLP yields $66$ candidate symmetry classes, of which exactly $15$ are realizable, supporting full projective diagonal logical cyclic groups of orders $2$, $3$, and $5$. In particular, for order $5$, the code is unique up to local unitaries and qubit permutations, equivalent to the code constructed in arXiv:2504.20847. This code also attains the minimum length $n=6$ among exact $((n, 2, \ge 3))$ codes whose full projective transversal group cannot be conjugated into the projective Clifford group.

title: Meter-scale quantum interconnects between large quantum processors
comment: 11 pages, 3 figures, 1 table, plus Extended Data
summary: Modular quantum architecture requires long-distance quantum interconnects to stitch together individual processor modules. Such interconnects, long-distance couplers or L-couplers, must support coherent quantum operation over meter-scale distances and scale to multiple connections between any two modules. Here we demonstrate four L-couplers operating between two 120-qubit IBM Nighthawk R1 superconducting qubit processors. Each L-coupler joins two Nighthawk lattice qubits through two frequency-tunable L-qubits, two RF-SQUID based "i2m" couplers, and 80 cm of superconducting aluminum coax. Each cable installs perpendicular to the processor surface, to enable denser connections, and is joined to the chip by an indium-to-indium room temperature pressure bond made after both modules were mounted. L-coupler modes near 5 GHz, with internal quality factors of 0.86 to 1.09e6, carry relay-based state transfer at a mean network benchmarking fidelity of 99.00%, with a best link of 99.29 +/- 0.07%. We then realize distant CZ gates between lattice qubits in separate modules at a mean fidelity of 94.75%, with a best link of 96.42 +/- 0.28%, and use them to generate entangled states across the two processors, including a demonstration of simultaneous Bell pair generation using two adjacent L-couplers. These four high-fidelity L-couplers establish a practical path to scalable quantum interconnects for modular quantum computing.

title: Two particle interference: The Hanbury Brown Twiss and Hong Ou Mandel experiments
comment: Chapter submitted to ''Comprehensive Quantum Physics'' to be published by Elsiever
summary: I discuss two important quantum optics experiments which depend on two particle interference. In the years since their first demonstration many interesting and instructive variants have appeared, including the use of atoms instead of photons as the interfering particles. This chapter gives a pedagogical overview of some of these results and argues that the two effects are closely related.

title: An entanglement band structure for general multiqubit states
summary: Majorana drew a symmetric multiqubit state as points on the Bloch sphere, antipodal to the zeros of its overlap with spin coherent states. Projecting only one qubit of a general state leaves the others in a state that varies with direction. Its entanglement invariants are eigenvalues of a non-Hermitian matrix and form bands over the sphere. Exceptional points appear, without gain or loss, where the entanglement family of the rest changes. Circling one exchanges two bands, so the bands form one Riemann surface. At five qubits it fixes the entanglement class up to finitely many choices.

title: High-fidelity and robust controlled-Z gates for superconducting transmon qubits. I. Intrinsic errors and decoherence
summary: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires quantum gates that combine short duration, high fidelity, and robustness to noise. As quantum processors scale, robustness becomes increasingly important because exhaustive characterization and frequent recalibration of individual gates become impractical. We present a comprehensive optimal-control framework for controlled-Z (CZ) gates between directly coupled, frequency-tunable transmons that systematically accounts for intrinsic Hamiltonian errors and realistic decoherence mechanisms, including energy relaxation and dephasing. Using smooth, single-shot flux pulses, we obtain 12-ns CZ gates---close to the theoretical speed limit of 11.6 ns---with intrinsic errors suppressed to the $2\times10^{-5}$ level. We construct dephasing noise models, calibrated against published experimental measurements, that capture fast dephasing from room-temperature control electronics and slow dephasing from $1/f$ flux noise. Using these models, we identify dephasing sweet spots that suppress sensitivity to dephasing noise. We further exploit transmon asymmetry as a design parameter to access distinct noise-resilient operating regimes. These results establish an experimentally applicable framework for balancing gate speed, fidelity, and noise robustness while reducing characterization and recalibration overhead.

title: Hydrodynamic description of correlation matrix eigenvalues in a finite temperature expanding free fermionic gas
summary: A recent work considered the Page curve for entanglement entropy of a freely expanding one-dimensional Fermi gas starting from a finite box (the system) in a zero-temperature initial state that then expands in to a semi-infinite vacuum (the environment). For the case with a single defect at the system-environment junction, it was shown that the Yang-Yang entropy of the system computed from semiclassical hydrodynamics agrees with the microscopically computed entanglement entropy, yielding the Page curve. On the other hand, the environment Yang-Yang entropy showed a monotonic increase. Here, we propose a hydrodynamic description to obtain the eigenvalues of the microscopic correlation matrix for a nonzero temperature freely-expanding Fermi gas. For the system, the phase space density directly gives the correlation matrix eigenvalues and thus, via the Yang-Yang formula, yields the von-Neumann entropy. For the reservoir, a modification of the phase space density is required in the Yang-Yang formula, to incorporate coherences, in order to reproduce accurately the entropy. The hydrodynamic description of correlation matrix eigenvalues also leads to a Levitov-Lesovik type formula for the full-counting-statistics for a finite system in the transient regime. We provide a heuristic derivation of the correlation matrix eigenvalues based on a semiclassical wave-packet picture.

title: A random sampling method to test the weak Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis
summary: We introduce a random sampling method for testing the weak Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis (wETH) that is particularly useful for large, sparse Hamiltonians. We test the method on a well-studied Rydberg atom system that exhibits both two- and three-body dipole-dipole interactions. Our results show that our method allows for the study of system sizes significantly beyond the limits of exact diagonalization. We find that the fluctuations in eigenstate expectation values decay as the Hilbert space dimension $D^{-1/2}$, consistent with wETH and in agreement with previous numerical results.

title: Injection is all you need: parallel universal logic in high-rate concatenated self-dual codes
summary: We propose a quantum architecture that achieves addressable and parallel universal fault-tolerant logical in high-rate codes. The codes are obtained from the flexible concatenation of small-distance high-rate self-dual CSS codes. Addressable and parallel universal logic on the resulting $K$ logical qubits is injected by fault-tolerantly preparing and then consuming diverse logical $K$-qubit CSS stabilizer states and logical $\lvert H \rangle^{\otimes K}$ global magic states. Flag-at-origin is used to prepare the stabilizer resource states while a concatenated cultivation protocol prepares the global magic states. These resource states are consumed by Steane-QEC or Knill-QEC teleportation gadgets, which simultaneously perform quantum error correction. Any quantum algorithm with $T$-depth $D_T$ can be executed by consuming $12D_T$ or fewer resource states. We benchmark the fault-tolerant preparation of the resource states for several two-level concatenations of the $[[k+4,k,2]]$ H codes and the Hamming $[[15,7,3]]$ code. In particular, we find that the concatenated cultivation offers at least one order of magnitude spacetime reduction compared to cultivation in the surface code.

title: The strengthened quantum Hamming bound of Yu, Lai, and Oh
comment: 106 pages; computational certificates and reproduction code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23535642
summary: We prove a conjecture of Yu, Lai, and Oh: their rounded family of strengthened quantum Hamming bounds, which interpolates between Hamming-type bounds and the Singleton bound, holds for arbitrary exact quantum subspaces of dimension $K>1$. The result covers every integer local dimension $p\ge2$, every integer $t\ge1$, both distances $2t+1$ and $2t+2$, and every interpolation parameter $e\in\{0,\ldots,t\}$. Yu, Lai, and Oh proved these bounds for pure codes and for general codes of distance three or four; the case $e=0$ contains the ordinary quantum Hamming bound for general codes, recently proved by Zhang and Chen. More generally, for $p\ge3$, we prove the inequality $Kf(0)\le p^n\mathbb{E}f(X)$, where $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,1-p^{-2})$, for every real polynomial $f$ of degree at most $D$, with $2\le D<d$, that is nonnegative on $\{0,\ldots,n\}$ and positive at zero; here $n$ and $d$ are the code length and distance.

title: Pure dephasing destroys two-photon amplitude, not nonlinear phase
summary: A two-level emitter chirally coupled to a waveguide imprints a $π$ conditional phase on a two-photon pulse, a key component assumed in quantum photonic neural network architectures, but whether it survives the pure dephasing of a solid-state emitter is unknown, since no two-photon scattering treatment includes it. We derive the dephased two-photon amplitude in closed form and validate it against an independent Fock-state master equation. The conditional phase is pinned at exactly $π$ at every dephasing rate examined: dephasing destroys the amplitude carrying the nonlinear phase rather than rotating it. The one- and two-photon channels are not attenuated equally, so dephasing does not simply scale the node down but reweights it between photon-number sectors---an error no phase setting can train away. The standard factorization of two-photon correlators, exact for arbitrary loss, fails at first order in $γ_φ$, discarding $16$--$81\%$ of pairs over $γ_φ/γ=0.1$--$1$.

title: Spectral signatures of hidden order and hidden quantum critical points
summary: Hidden-order phases elude the conventional Ginzburg-Landau framework: although they spontaneously break symmetry, their order remains invisible to standard local two-point correlators. Instead, they are typically characterized by nonlocal (string) order parameters and are believed to underlie a range of exotic quantum states, such as symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases. While hidden correlations have previously been detected through nonlocal observables in quantum gas microscope experiments, in realistic solid-state systems multipoint observables are typically inaccessible and the signatures of hidden order remain largely unexplored. In this work, we show that hidden order in doped spin chains can be directly probed through dynamical two-point response functions measurable by resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) and neutron scattering. Focusing on a minimal model, we numerically identify clear spectral fingerprints of both the hidden-order phase, its associated hidden quantum critical point as well as a specific group of gapless SPT phases. Complementing our numerical results with analytical insights, we uncover the microscopic origin of these spectral signatures and demonstrate how they emerge from the interplay between spin and charge degrees of freedom. Together, our results establish spectroscopy as a practical probe of hidden order and gapless SPT phases and provide a unified understanding of the low-energy physics governing these unconventional quantum phases.

title: Algebraic criteria for complete relaxation in autonomous and periodically driven open quantum systems
summary: We derive sufficient criteria that guarantee convergence of open quantum system dynamics to a unique long-time state independent of the initial conditions. We refer to this behavior as complete relaxation. Focusing on systems described by Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad (GKSL) master equations on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, our approach uses only elementary mathematical arguments. For autonomous systems, we recover three previously derived relaxation criteria, which can be expressed as algebraic conditions on the Lindblad operators and the Hamiltonian entering the GKSL equation. For periodically driven systems, we obtain a new criterion involving a similar algebraic condition and a local continuity requirement on the time-dependent GKSL generator. This result implies an earlier criterion for complete relaxation formulated in Ref. [J. Phys. A 52, 43LT01 (2019)]. We also discuss implications of our approach for periodically modulated classical master equations, as well as extensions to driven systems without a periodicity constraint.

title: Geometry-controlled zeros of resonant Kelvin-wave conversion in four spatial dimensions
summary: Kelvin waves carry energy along vortices, but their resonant interactions contain information that is absent from the linear spectrum. We identify a geometry that exposes this information on a vortex surface in four spatial dimensions. Perpendicular incoming waves cancel the complete local-area four-wave coupling, leaving the finite nonlocal interaction mediated by the surrounding fluid. This interaction restores conversion at generic wave-number ratios, yet changes sign and vanishes at a selected ratio while momentum and frequency remain exactly matched. Matching to Gross-Pitaevskii (GP) theory, including the microscopic core response, establishes a zero of the full coupling at every sufficiently small nonzero wave number, with ratio tending to $λ_*\simeq1.469$. Finite-grid GP coefficients exhibit a sign reversal for the same resonant quartets. Separate coherent-mixing calculations and weak-probe spectra connect the coupling sign to the generated-wave phase and the ordering of reflection-even and reflection-odd modes. The resulting suppression removes a leading channel for changing propagation directions without changing the paired wavelengths. These results isolate a nonlinear effect of the surrounding flow that local tension misses, providing a microscopic benchmark for vortex-wave theories and a starting point for studying angular redistribution beyond the Kelvin spectrum.

title: Splitting Probability in Monitored Quantum Dynamics
summary: We consider a continuous-time quantum walk stroboscopically subjected to projective measurements on two distinct targets with sampling time period $τ$. We construct a general renewal framework for the first-detection amplitude at each target, from which we obtain the associated splitting probabilities. For Hamiltonians with reflection symmetry, we further show that each dual-target first-detection amplitude can be viewed as an interference effect between a pair of single-target first-detection amplitudes. This formulation yields exact expressions for the splitting probabilities and gives special sampling times at which they undergo pointwise discontinuous jumps due to a form of ergodicity breaking associated with dark states. As an illustrative example, we apply the framework to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice chain with nearest-neighbor hopping, and study the splitting probabilities as functions of the initial position and sampling time. Below a critical sampling time, $0<τ< τ_c$ where $τ_c = 2 π/ ΔE$ with $ΔE$ being the energy bandwidth, the splitting probabilities for large system sizes become equal to $1/2$, independent of the initial position, as long as this position does not coincide with target sites. Above the critical sampling time, $τ\geq τ_c$, the splitting probabilities deviate from $1/2$ and develop oscillations as a function of initial position. The wavenumber associated with these oscillations is $Q=2\sin^{-1}(rτ_c/τ)$, where $r$ is a positive integer. We also explore the effects of relative phase and spatial separation between different components of a coherent initial state on the splitting probabilities. Finally, we study how a finite number of measurements modifies the splitting probabilities and broadens the resonances at special sampling times.

title: From Traveling Waves to Synthetic Gauge Fields: A Field-Free Route to Superconducting Diode Effect
summary: The superconducting diode effect requires the forward and reverse bias currents to differ, a scenario achieved via inversion and time-reversal symmetries broken together. The latter, and the more crucial one, is inevitably achieved by a magnetic field. Here, we show that a spatio-temporally driven chemical potential of the form, $μ_j(t)=μ+V\cos(ωt+\kd j)$, achieves both at once. Applied to a helical Shiba chain, the drive transmutes a traveling Peierls phase via generating an odd-in-momentum term, equivalent to an imaginary next-nearest-neighbour Haldane-like hopping in real space. Remarkably, the protocol is spin-blind, which renders the time-reversal breaking via a synthetic gauge flux rather than an effective Zeeman field. The rectification is odd in the drive wavevector, with exact zeros at $\kd=nπ$ and an analytical optimum at $\kd=2π/3$. It is however, even in the exchange coupling, $J$ and persists even at $J=0$. Furthermore, the rectification scales inversely with the pair-breaking gap, yielding approximately $50\%$ rectification in the topological phase and $10\%$ in the trivial phase. Symmetry breaking is thus drive-controlled, allowing it to be switched on, tuned, and reversed without an external magnetic field.
